resources.string: Disclaimer: This app provides preliminary screening only and does not replace professional dental diagnosis.
Urgent: Visit a dentist within 2 weeks
Visit a dentist within 1 to 3 months
Keep up your routine and mention this at your next check-up
Visit a dentist within the next 2 weeks, and sooner if you feel pain, swelling or sensitivity.
Book a dentist appointment within the next 1 to 3 months.
Mention these findings at your next routine dental check-up (every 6 months).
Cut back on sugary and acidic foods and drinks, especially between meals and before bed.
Brush the affected teeth gently with fluoride toothpaste, and avoid chewing hard foods on them until a dentist has checked them.
Book a professional cleaning (scaling): tartar cannot be removed by brushing at home.
Brush along the gumline twice a day and use an antibacterial mouthwash to slow new buildup.
Brush gently along the gumline twice a day and floss daily to remove plaque. Bleeding gums often improve with regular, gentle cleaning.
Rinse with an antibacterial mouthwash, and avoid smoking and tobacco while your gums heal.
Brush for 2 minutes, twice a day, with fluoride toothpaste.
Floss daily and drink plenty of water, especially after meals.
Step %1$d is done, tap to undo
Sugary snacks and drinks feed the bacteria that cause cavities. Keep sweets to mealtimes rather than all day, and rinse with water afterwards.
Use a fluoride toothpaste twice a day. Fluoride helps repair early enamel damage and makes teeth more resistant to acid. Avoid rinsing with water straight after brushing.
Cavities do not heal on their own.
Decay does not reverse once it has gone through the enamel. A small filling now is much simpler than a root canal later, so book a visit soon.
Only a dentist can remove tartar.
Hardened tartar sticks to teeth and can only be removed by professional scaling. Brushing harder will not remove it and can damage your gums.
Angle the brush toward the gums.
Hold the brush at about 45 degrees to the gumline and use short, gentle strokes. Tartar builds up fastest behind the lower front teeth.
A professional cleaning about every 6 months stops tartar from building up and protects your gums.
Use a soft toothbrush and light pressure along the gumline. Brushing too hard can make gums recede.
Floss once a day between all teeth, curving the floss around each tooth. Your gums may bleed at first, which usually settles within a couple of weeks.
Do not ignore bleeding or swelling.
Red, swollen or bleeding gums, or persistent bad breath, mean the inflammation is still active. See a dentist if they do not improve.
Regular check-ups catch problems early, when treatment is simplest. Make a visit every 6 months a habit.
